quotes.text: SLA timers start late then expire quietly. No one notices until the callback is angry. You don't miss emails. You miss intent.
quotes.speaker: Mirko Peters
quotes.why: Reframes the support inbox problem as missed intent rather than missed messages.

quotes.text: The backlog isn't a volume problem. It's a design problem. Fix intake. Then everything downstream starts to look sane.
quotes.speaker: Mirko Peters
quotes.why: States the episode's core thesis that intake design drives service quality.

quotes.text: Autonomous agents do this work without blinking. But only if you give them structure. Identity, taxonomy, entitlements and routes. Otherwise you just automate the mess faster.
quotes.speaker: Mirko Peters
quotes.why: Names the prerequisites autonomous agents need to add value.

quotes.text: Poor data quality kills automation quietly. Dirty categories. Stale product lists. Missing entitlements. The agent can't map to truth if your truth is rotten.
quotes.speaker: Mirko Peters
quotes.why: Concrete warning about data quality as the main pitfall of AI-driven case handling.

quotes.text: AI isn't replacing your agents. It's deleting the backlog and binding identity. So humans can make the real calls.
quotes.speaker: Mirko Peters
quotes.why: Clarifies the human role in AI-supported customer service.

chapters.title: The hidden costs of manual processing
Governance and security in AI-powered support
Real-world results, pitfalls and a 30-60-90 plan

takeaways: Customer service chaos comes from an ungoverned email-to-case intake path, not from email volume itself.
Autonomous agents in Dynamics 365 read, classify and create cases, route them with unified routing by skills, capacity and SLA, and let Copilot draft responses for human review.
Clean taxonomy, identity binding, audit logs, PII redaction and DLP must be in place first, otherwise automation only speeds up existing mistakes.
hook: Overflowing support inboxes, late SLA clocks and misrouted tickets are a design problem, not a staffing problem. This episode is for customer service leaders and Dynamics 365 teams who want to fix intake without burning out their agents. You will learn how autonomous agents, unified routing and Copilot drafts work together under governance, plus the pitfalls and a 30-60-90 rollout plan.
